title: Uways al-Qarani
hook: a man from Yemen who never met the Prophet ﷺ, cared for his mother, and whose prayers were sought
tomorrow: The women who asked for a day

segments.voice: Yesterday: Sa'd, the chief of the Ansar. Your line was the throne shook.

Every time a fresh group of fighters arrives in Medina from Yemen, Umar ibn al-Khattab goes out to meet them with the same question. Is Uways ibn Amir among you? Again and again, no. Umar leads the whole community by now, and still he keeps asking after one man he has never seen. Then one day a voice in the crowd says yes. Umar walks up to him and asks his own favor: pray for me. Today: Uways al-Qarani.
screen: `IS UWAYS AMONG YOU?` → `AGAIN AND AGAIN, NO.` → `THEN ONE DAY, YES.`

segments.voice: The story is in Sahih Muslim, and Umar tells us why he kept asking. He had heard the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, describe a man who would come with the reinforcements from Yemen: Uways ibn Amir, of the tribe of Murad, then of the clan of Qaran. He had suffered a skin disease and been cured of it, except for one small patch. And he had a mother, and he was devoted to her. Then something remarkable: if this man swore by God, God would make his oath come true. If you meet him, ask him to seek forgiveness for you. So Umar checks every detail, and Uways confirms them all: Murad, Qaran, the healed skin, the mother. Then Umar, the companion of the Prophet, asks a man who never met the Prophet to pray for him. And Uways does. Why did he never meet him? The hadith only says he was dutiful to his mother. Tradition says that is exactly what kept him in Yemen: she needed him, and he stayed. That link is the tradition's, not the hadith's words. Then the end of the conversation. Umar asks where he is going. Kufa, says Uways. Umar offers to write to the governor there for him, and Uways declines. He would rather be among the ordinary people, the ones nobody notices. He had a recommendation from the leader of the believers in his hand, and he let it go. The man whose prayer was sought was the man who did not seek to be seen. And in the Prophet's description, the one deed named is not a battle or a speech. It is his care for his mother.
screen: `DESCRIBED BY THE PROPHET.` · `DEVOTED TO HIS MOTHER.` · `UMAR ASKS HIM TO PRAY.` · `HE CHOOSES TO STAY UNNOTICED.` · then, large: `HE STAYED WITH HIS MOTHER.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind your mother or father, or whoever raised you, and one ordinary thing they need right now: a call, a ride, a meal, ten minutes of listening without your phone. If your parent has died, hold them in mind instead and, if you pray, ask mercy for them. If the relationship is hard, choose something small and safe, or simply wish them well.
Uways al-Qarani. A man of Qaran in Yemen, devoted to his mother, described by the Prophet, and sought out by Umar for his prayer. Today's word.
Your line: he stayed with his mother. Unseen, and still sought out. That's day eight hundred fifty-seven.

'Leader of the believers' (amir al-mu'minin) for Umar and 'fighters/reinforcements' (amdad) from Yemen: confirm wording.
The patch of skin is described in the hadith as the size of a dirham; the script says 'one small patch'.
